intro: Lesson 20: What is the Earth like inside? A cracked Earth. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

box.title: Draw the Earth as circles inside each other and label: crust, mantle, outer core, inner core

picture.alt: World map of the tectonic plates and their boundaries
picture.draw: Draw the main plate boundaries and label six plates

panels.title: The layers
points: Mantle: hot rock that flows slowly
Outer core: liquid iron and nickel
Inner core: solid, about 5,000°C or more

panels.title: A cracked Earth
points: The crust is broken into plates
Earthquakes and volcanoes follow plate edges
The Ring of Fire circles the Pacific

parts.text: The core heats the lower mantle
Hot rock rises slowly and spreads
The moving mantle drags the plates; slab pull also pulls sinking plates down

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: A four-step explanation of plate movement

keywords.def: the thin, solid outer layer of the Earth
the thick layer of hot rock below the crust
the hot iron and nickel centre of the Earth
a large piece of the Earth's broken crust
a loop of heat rising and sinking in the mantle

questions.q: What is the Ring of Fire?
questions.a: A belt of volcanoes and earthquakes around the Pacific
Pacific, Eurasian, African, North American, Indo-Australian, Nazca

questions.q: Core: Draw and label a cross-section of the Earth, then write a paragraph explaining how plates move, using convection, ridge push and slab pull.
questions.a: Accurate labelled diagram and a correct explanation

questions.q: Extend: Compare the world maps of earthquakes and plates: describe the pattern.
questions.a: Earthquakes cluster along plate boundaries, especially around the Pacific

questions.q: Stretch: How do scientists know about layers they cannot see?
questions.a: Seismic waves change speed and direction through different layers

questions.q: Which crust is denser and can sink?
questions.a: B) Oceanic. Oceanic crust (basalt) is denser, so it sinks beneath continental crust.

questions.q: Big question: what is happening under the 'apple skin'?
questions.a: Convection in the hot mantle slowly moves the cracked plates
